chunks: Abu Abdillah al-'Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbat, from al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm, from Abu al-Hasan al-Ridha (peace be upon him), who said:

Our companions were mentioned in his presence, and the intellect was (also) mentioned. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No regard is given to the people of the religion from those who have no intellect.'
I said: 'May I be your ransom! Indeed among those who profess this matter (al-Wilayah), there is a group who are not found faulty in our view, yet they do not possess those intellects.'

So he said: 'These are not among those whom God addressed. Indeed, God created the intellect and said to it: Come forward! So it came forward. And said to it: Turn back! So it turned back. Then He said: By My might and My majesty! I have not created anything better than you, nor more beloved to Me than you. Through you I take (hold accountable), and through you I give (reward).'

key_terms.العقل: The intellect/reason — not merely cognitive ability but a divinely-gifted spiritual faculty that enables moral accountability and response to divine address
key_terms.لا يُعبأ: No regard is given to / is not counted among — indicating exclusion from the scope of divine address and accountability
key_terms.من خاطب الله: Those whom God addressed — the morally accountable, those capable of receiving divine guidance
key_terms.هذا الأمر: This matter — a technical phrase referring to the Imamate and Wilayah, the recognition of the rightful Imam
key_terms.وعزتي وجلالي: By My might and My majesty — a divine oath formula emphasizing the absolute nature of what follows

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha say about God creating the intellect in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (AS) teaches that the intellect ('aql) is the criterion for religious accountability — those without true intellect are not among those whom God addresses. The Imam narrates a primordial cosmological account of God creating the intellect and testing its obedience before declaring it the most beloved of all creation. This hadith is from the foundational chapter on the intellect in al-Kafi, reflecting the central importance of rational capacity in Shia theology. The questioner al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm was a close companion of the Imam who regularly asked him theological questions.

en.hubeali:
Abu Abdullah Al Aasimy, from Ali Bin Al Hassan, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Al Hassan Bin Al Jahm, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘Our companions were mentioned in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, and the intellect was (also) mentioned. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not package (consider as the same) the people of the Religion from the one who has not intellect for him’.

I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! From the ones who are described to be upon this matter (Al-Wilayah), there is a group for whom there a no problems with them in our presence, and there isn’t that (kind of) intellect for them’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are not from the ones whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Addressed. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Created the intellect, so He<sup>azwj</sup> Said to it: “Come!” So it came. And Said to it: “Turn back!” So it turned back. So He<sup>azwj</sup> Said: ‘By M<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and My<sup>azwj</sup> majesty! I<sup>azwj</sup> have not Created anything better than you, or more Beloved to Me<sup>azwj</sup> than you. Due to you, I<sup>azwj</sup> shall Seize, and due to you I<sup>azwj</sup> shall Give’.
